prompt: An algorithms lecture slide shows a small undirected graph of 7 nodes labelled with letters A through G, drawn as circles connected by edges. The edges are: A-B, A-D, A-E, B-C, C-F, D-F, E-G, F-G. Run a BREADTH-FIRST SEARCH starting from node A. When exploring a node's neighbours, always visit them in ALPHABETICAL order. Number the nodes 1, 2, 3 ... in the exact ORDER that BFS first visits them (A is visited first, so A gets 1). Render the same graph and write the BFS visit-order NUMBER large inside each node's circle, keeping the node letter small in a corner. Do NOT write the adjacency list, a queue, or any other numbers on the slide.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show algorithms lecture slide of a 7-node letter-labelled graph with each node's breadth-first visit-order number written large inside its circle? Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.
